best.rationale: y2 proposes an identifiable change to ref-060: learn a failure predictor combining gradient norms with softmax confidence, with component ablations and evaluation across shift severities. x1 specifies a plausible experiment, but ref-002 already proposes flat minima for failure prediction and combines two flat-minima techniques; ref-059 already evaluates covariate shift and long tails. Its remaining contribution is therefore poorly established. y2 still needs held-out corruption splits and a continuous evaluation score, and its attribution of particular corruption datasets and covariate-shift findings to ref-007/ref-008 is unsupported by the supplied abstracts.

worst.rationale: y3 substantially overlaps ref-002/ref-059, and the supplied abstract does not substantiate its claim that ref-002 excludes SAM plus SWA. Nevertheless, its SAM-only, SWA-only, and combined ablations provide a concrete experiment. x3 reproduces SIRC from ref-005 without a clear modification and misstates its motivation: ref-005 explicitly says conflating incorrect ID predictions with OOD samples is acceptable, whereas x3 presents that conflation as the problem. Its restriction of the auxiliary information to the output distribution is also unsupported. These grounding and coherence problems make x3 weaker.

diversity.rationale: Both sets span three substantially different approaches: training-time flat-minima optimization, representation learning for OOD detection, and confidence-signal combination. X uses hyperspherical geometry and post-hoc SCOD scoring; Y uses reconstruction pretraining and a learned gradient/softmax predictor under shift. Neither set consists merely of parameter variations, and their differences do not establish a meaningful diversity advantage. Repetition of cited methods reduces originality but does not erase the differences among these approaches.

overall.rationale: Y offers the more useful research choice because y2 has a discernible intervention beyond its closest cited method and experiments capable of testing its added value. X largely restates existing contributions: flat-minima failure prediction in ref-002/ref-059, CIDER in ref-029, and SIRC in ref-005. Y is imperfect: y1 overlaps MOOD in ref-036 and inconsistently describes a no-fine-tuning gap while including fine-tuning, and y3 asserts an unverified distinction from ref-002. Even with those weaknesses, Y supplies one reasonably actionable new hypothesis and stronger component comparisons.
